blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: While one thread is partway through a for-each over a `ConcurrentHashMap`'s entries, another thread puts a new key into it. Per this page, what can the first thread's loop do?

options.text: It may or may not reach the new key, and it throws no exception
options.says: The page says weakly consistent iterators never throw ConcurrentModificationException and may reflect some, all, or none of the modifications made after their creation.

options.text: It throws ConcurrentModificationException at its next step
options.says: The page says weakly consistent iterators are guaranteed not to throw ConcurrentModificationException.

options.text: It is sure to reach the new key, as it reads the live table
options.says: The page says such an iterator may reflect some, all, or none of the later modifications, so reaching the new key is not guaranteed.

questions.stem: Code calls `remove()` on an iterator of a `CopyOnWriteArrayList`, right after a `next()`. Per this page, what happens?

options.text: It throws UnsupportedOperationException, and the list keeps the element
options.says: The page says snapshot iterators do NOT support remove(), set() or add(): they throw UnsupportedOperationException.

options.text: It throws ConcurrentModificationException, and the list keeps the element
options.says: The page says CopyOnWriteArrayList iterators never throw ConcurrentModificationException.

options.text: It removes the element from the list, though the iterator still holds it
options.says: The page says the iterator's remove() is not supported at all; the list's own remove is the fix.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A CopyOnWriteArrayList iterator does not support remove(), which throws UnsupportedOperationException; the list's own remove or removeIf is used instead.
A ConcurrentHashMap iterator is weakly consistent: it never throws, returns each element at most once, and may or may not show writes made after it was created.
